properties.name: One reflow2 can hold several designs, and a session says which one it is working on
properties.statement: A person works on more than one project at a time, so reflow2 must be able to hold more than one design without their contents mixing, and a session must state which design it is operating on before it can read or write. Anthony, 2026-07-25: he has reflow2 itself and storyflow; his brother has several. Three properties follow. Selection is EXPLICIT — a session that has not named its design must be refused rather than defaulted to the last one used or the only one present, because a tool call landing in the wrong project is a silent corruption that no gap detector would ever notice. Segregation is enforced by the store, not by convention: every node and edge already carries a graph_id, which is exactly the primitive this needs, and today it is pinned to the constant "reflow2" — so the mechanism exists and is unused, the same shape as the temporal axis and the inviolable-intent vocabulary before them. And the identity of a design must be stable across machines, so the same project reached from two places is one design rather than two that happen to share a name. This is deliberately silent on where the designs live: one process per design and one holding many are both answers to it, and that is the hosting question, not this requirement.
